Wick Gull.narrative: I've fished this harbour since I was a boy, and I know every tide and every debt on the quay. Since the Surge I go out with my gut tight, and I come back loud to cover it. Bramwell Tallow's rope is on my tally and I'll pay it with the next good catch, but he's begun to say so at the stalls, and that stings more than the wind. Nia keeps the night crews fed; I keep us afloat, or try to.
values: a good catch over a full boat of talk
my own boat and my own name
goals: bring in a catch big enough to clear the rope debt
keep Bramwell Tallow from saying it aloud at the stalls again
see the lower quay rebuilt so the small boats have shelter
keep Dory away from the dark water
learn the harbour's western shallows well enough to set a new line of pots
take Dory out on the calm water some fine morning and teach her the oars
Wick Gull.mood: shamed and blustering, with a knot in the gut when the wind rises

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows the marks are short before I do, and she says it gently, which is worse.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Afraid of the dark water like I am, and I don't want her to learn it from me.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He's owed and I know it. But a man who duns you at the stalls wants an audience, not a mark.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: Sharp about the price of everything, and she keeps the tally where Bramwell can see it.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We drink together and curse the stone price together. He'd patch the quay with salvage and call it done.

relations.name: Ostrander Gull
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: My uncle mends nets and remembers every boat the Surge took. He doesn't need to say it; I know.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay and I'll mind her word, but the lower quay wants stone, not speeches.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Keeps the lamp oil and the dried fish; says the tide lanterns are lit too late, and she's right.

relations.name: Wick Brine
relations.label: guard
relations.note: Walks the night road and knows the smugglers' paths. Useful to know, and he knows it.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: cook
relations.note: Fries fish by the market and wants her stall in stone. Good bread, sharp tongue.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall-holder
relations.note: Nia works beside her; her noodles keep the night crews standing.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: quay scribe
relations.note: He writes the tide lantern list; I'd rather he wrote my name off Bramwell's slate.

relations.name: Rook Fenner
relations.label: fellow fisher
relations.note: North-shore accent, tarred boat, owes Cormorant a net share — we're all of us a little short.

memories.gist: The night the Surge came I was on the quay and saw the lower houses go; I got my boat out and nothing else.
Bramwell Tallow sold me rope and tar on a promise after a bad month, and I was glad of it then.
A good catch last spring filled the boat and the stall both, and I paid a debt that day and felt tall.
Dory wouldn't go near the tide steps for a week after she saw a swell take a bucket; I carried her home.
Bramwell said my name loud across the stalls this month, and half the quay turned to look.

stances.why: A debt is a debt, but a man dunned at the stalls loses the custom that would pay it.
I saw the lower quay go in one night; the sea doesn't owe anyone a good catch.
Nobody who hasn't shared a boat with me gets a say in my affairs.
The Warden talks of a seawall, but the small boats need shelter now, and I say so.
She's afraid of it, and I'd rather she stayed afraid than careless.

Wick Gull.secret: I've been out past the harbour mouth on the ebb more than once when the catch was short, in water I shouldn't fish and near the Cormorants' grounds, and I'd not say so to Ostrander Cormorant.
pastimes: mending nets and tarring rope on the quay at first light
telling tall tales of old catches to the night crews over a mug
walking the seawall at dusk to read the weather
Wick Gull.calling: I'm a fisherman, and a good one; the sea's the only work I've ever wanted.

Nia Gull.narrative: I cook at a stall on the quay and feed the night crews, and I know to a mark what comes in and what goes out. Wick owes Bramwell Tallow for rope and tar, and the marks are short until a good catch; I'd have Bramwell wait, and I fear what Wick's temper will say before I can. I work beside Ilse Ostrander, and I think the Warden should have put the lower quay back before anything else.
values: a full pot over a proud word
keeping the peace at the stalls
goals: stretch the marks until Wick's next good catch
keep Wick and Bramwell from a quarrel in the open
keep Dory fed and out from under the stalls
save enough marks for a proper stall with a roof and a second pot
see Dory Quell and Dory play together more often, and the two families share a meal
Nia Gull.mood: steady but tired, counting marks in her head

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: husband
relations.note: Loud when he's shamed and quiet when he's afraid, and I can tell which before he speaks.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She plays under the stalls where I can see her, and that's the only reason I let her.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He's owed and he's been patient, but saying it loud at the stalls won't fill his purse.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She keeps her marks in her apron and her eye on everyone's; she knows our tally to the mark.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: We work the same row and she's had her grief; I'd not have her hear Wick's debt from another mouth.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay, and I'd follow her, but the lower quay should have come first.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She sells me lamp oil and thinks the lanterns are lit too late; she's not wrong.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He drinks with Wick and talks of the seawall; at least he does something with his hands.

relations.name: Dory Quell
relations.label: child's friend
relations.note: She and my Dory play together under the stalls; the Warden's house is a strange place for a child.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: cook
relations.note: Works the fish market beside me; wants her stall in stone, and I'd not say no to that myself.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She treats the coughs of the quay; I've sent her more than one night-crew hand.

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She keeps the soup and bread stall by the tide steps for the early boats; we trade the night crews back and forth and she never quibbles over a mark.

relations.name: Ostrander Gull
relations.label: kin by marriage
relations.note: Wick's uncle mends nets and remembers every boat the Surge took; he grumbles at Kettlebridge for the seawall stone and I let him, but he's no help with the rope debt.

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay and the houses on it; I was cooking for the night crews and we fed whoever came up wet.
Wick brought home a good catch last spring and we paid a debt and ate well the same week.
Dory was small enough to sleep in the stall's crate while I cooked, and the crews kept their voices down for her.
Bramwell said Wick's name loud across the stalls, and I watched the fishers turn and listen.
Ilse's knees have gone bad and she still stands the whole night at her stall; I take her a bowl when I can.

stances.why: The crews eat at my stall and the quay runs on them; a short bowl is a short night.
Bramwell knows the sea; a fisher can't pay from an empty boat.
The small boats lost their shelter in the Surge and the Warden talks of stone walls.
His temper would make the debt a quarrel, and a quarrel costs custom.
We share what we have with those who share the boats; the rest can wait.

Nia Gull.secret: I've sold a bowl or two on credit to crews who never paid, and I've not told Wick, because he'd shout it at the stalls and make it worse.
pastimes: singing old harbour songs while the pot simmers
trading gossip and recipes with Ilse and Nia Brine at the stalls
walking the quay at dusk to watch the lanterns lit for the drowned
Nia Gull.calling: I feed the night crews, and I'd have it no other way; a full pot is my craft.

Dory Gull.narrative: I play under the stalls where Mama can see me, and I know the gulls' names and which boards are loose. The tide steps are dark and the water goes down and down, and I don't go near them. Dory Quell plays with me and we hide from the night crews.
values: the dry boards under the stalls
goals: find a gull's nest without falling
stay away from the dark water
find a gull's nest all by herself
learn all the loose boards under the stalls by heart
Dory Gull.mood: happy, and watchful near the water

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and fish and I can find her by it.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lifts me high and his coat is wet and cold and I laugh.

relations.name: Dory Quell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play under the stalls and she knows the gulls too.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: stall-neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the lamp oil next to our stall and lets me hold the little bottles if I'm careful.

relations.name: Ostrander Gull
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He sits mending nets and tells me what the water took; his voice is slow and I sit close.

memories.gist: A swell took my bucket off the tide steps and I ran all the way to Mama's stall.
Papa carried me on his shoulders past the lanterns and I could see all the boats at once.

pastimes: playing hide-and-seek under the stalls with Dory Quell
collecting smooth stones and shells from the dry boards
watching the gulls and naming them
Dory Gull.calling: When I'm big I want to cook at the stall like Mama.
